canonical_statement: For a field K, stable matrix equivalence classes of finite-dimensional central simple K-algebras form an abelian group: multiplication is induced by tensor product, the class of K is the identity, and the opposite algebra represents the inverse.

canonical_formal_target.declaration_or_expression_candidate: an inhabitant of BrauerGroupAbelianLawData for every field K, after exact comparison with the human source

domain_and_universes: K is a field; A and B range over finite-dimensional central simple K-algebras; Lean universe levels and size constraints remain to be frozen
quantifiers: for all central simple K-algebra representatives A and B where required
hypotheses: representatives are finite-dimensional central simple K-algebras
conclusion: Brauer-equivalence classes carry the stated abelian group law with tensor, base-field, and opposite-algebra representatives
boundary_cases: split matrix algebras represent the identity class
zero-dimensional or nonunital algebras are excluded by the central-simple-algebra object
commutative base rings beyond fields are excluded

alternate_encodings.target: BrauerClass A = BrauerClass B iff IsBrauerEquivalent A B
alternate_encodings.relationship: quotient equality consequence, strictly weaker than construction of the group law

alternate_encodings.target: each CSA is a matrix algebra over a division algebra
alternate_encodings.relationship: Artin-Wedderburn supporting normal form, not the root theorem

excluded_claims: Brauer group of an arbitrary commutative ring or scheme
classification up to algebra isomorphism rather than stable equivalence
